label: rem:im-q-vs-p-skew
title: Im(q) is not the EM / P_skew channel — distinct mechanisms
html:
The framework has two distinct projection mechanisms that each discard structural content. They are often conflated, yet must be kept separate:

Two mechanisms

Mechanism 1 — bar projection (real-q phenomenon)

Per bar-involution.md, every Hecke-algebra element decomposes as x = P_{\mathrm{avg}}(x) + P_{\mathrm{skew}}(x) under the bar involution q \mapsto q^{-1} (equivalently \eta = \log q \mapsto -\eta). The framework's canonical projection is P_{\mathrm{avg}} (bar-symmetric, \cos/\cosh/\mathrm{Li}_2^q content); the bar-anti-symmetric P_{\mathrm{skew}} (\sin/\sinh/\Phi_q content) is discarded by construction.

For real q > 0, \eta = \log q is real, \sinh(\eta) is a real number, and P_{\mathrm{skew}} content is real-valued. For torus knots this is explicit: Q_m(\eta) = \sinh((2m+1)\eta) / (2 \cosh \eta) is real at real q_0. Per crossing-energy-interpretation.md, \sinh(\log q) is the EM / Coulomb channel. So the EM / P_skew content exists for real q and is discarded by the canonical projection.

Mechanism 2 — modulus projection (complex-q phenomenon)

Per prop:categorical-mass-markov, the categorical mass formula is

\mathfrak{m}_{q, \mathcal{K}} = \mathrm{tr}_M(\rho(\beta_\mathcal{K})).

The |\cdot| is the modulus. For real q, \mathrm{tr}_M is real and |\cdot| is trivial (absolute value of a sign). For complex q, \mathrm{tr}_M becomes complex and |\cdot| genuinely projects: \mathrm{Im}(\mathrm{tr}_M) is discarded.

A common incorrect claim

A natural-but-incorrect claim is "Im(q) = EM channel = P_skew channel". This conflates the two mechanisms. The correct statements are:

Quantity Source Status at real q
P_{\mathrm{skew}} content (sinh, EM channel) bar projection Real-valued, non-zero, discarded
\mathrm{Im}(q) content complex-q parameter Zero by convention (q real); would generate complex tr_M if non-zero
\mathrm{Im}(\mathrm{tr}_M) content modulus projection Zero by convention for real q; generated by Im(q) \ne 0

So:

  • P_skew is kept then discarded by the framework even at real q.
  • Im(q) is set to zero by the framework's real-q convention, not "discarded by a projection".
  • These are independent.

Significance

Quantitative consequences differ between the two mechanisms:

  1. Resolving the +0.17% \mathfrak{Q}_\beta residual: this requires either (a) the missing P_skew content at real q (the P_skew channel that bar-projection discards), or (b) Im(q) \ne 0 producing complex tr_M whose modulus closes the residual.

    • (b) is ruled out under the current ansatz (residual is positive everywhere on the Apollonius circle).
    • (a) is open — accessible via the explicit Q_m P_skew content given above.

  2. Resolving the canonical lepton-mass formula F_\ell(q) (conj:lepton-mass-tower-canonical): the ratio |\mathrm{tr}_M(K_\mu)| / |\mathrm{tr}_M(K_e)| is robust against \mathrm{Im}(q) at leading order (modulus projection invariance), but NOT robust against the bar-projection discarding P_{\mathrm{skew}} content (the discarded sinh-channel could shift the LO ratio).

  3. Physical interpretation: P_{\mathrm{skew}} = EM/charge-distinguishing channel (explicit for torus knots, as above). \mathrm{Im}(q) = a substrate moduli parameter (not directly physical until tied to an Im-sensitive observable, which the framework does not currently provide).
